subject: Benchmark grant routing & allocation — HealthLytics bake-off
messages:
From: Nikesh Patel <npatel@healthlytics.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthLytics Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: trial funding and allocation for bake-off vs ZephyrAI

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers on sparse-sequence reranking looked promising. Our procurement team has one ask before we proceed to the technical bake-off: can Redwood provide a discrete evaluation grant that covers the compute for a 3-week benchmark (multi-model comparison vs ZephyrAI and an in-house baseline)? We need a clear allocation that we can include in the SOW so finance can sign off.

Scope: 3 weeks, up to 500k token-equivalents across generation + embeddings, access to logs for evaluation (anonymized), and a single canary rollback window. Attached is the RFP scope doc for reference.

Budget owners prefer vendor-provided credits vs purchase order for this stage. Is there a standard grant routing approach you use for competitive RFPs with procurement? Any constraints we should expect (SLA, usage caps, expiration)?

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Nikesh
Director of AI Engineering
HealthLytics

Attachment: HealthLytics_RFP_Scope.pdf (pdf, 240KB)

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Nikesh Patel <npatel@healthlytics.com>
Cc: HealthLytics Procurement <procurement@healthlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: trial funding and allocation for bake-off vs ZephyrAI

Nikesh — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear scope. We can support a vendor-funded evaluation grant model for competitive bake-offs. High level proposal:

- Allocation: $25k equivalent in Redwood credits (roughly maps to the 500k token-equivalents you listed)
- Duration: 30-day activation window to allow the team to schedule a 3-week run
- Controls: per-route rate caps and a single audit log export (anonymized) for the evaluation team
- SLA: hosted eval has standard availability (we can sign a short addendum for a 99.5% uptime promise for the evaluation period)
- Competitive terms: we require a short non-exclusive benchmarking notice (30 days) and attribution for public materials if results are published

If that sounds reasonable, I will route for approval and share a mutual action plan (dates, contact list, kickoff tasks). I can also include a fallback policy (auto-switch to smaller-quantized model) if usage exceeds the estimate to avoid surprise overages.

Would procurement like the credit to be issued to a named HubSpot deal so it appears on your SOW & purchase reconciliation?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-grant-proposal-v1.xlsx (xlsx, 95KB)

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: trial funding and allocation for bake-off vs ZephyrAI

Ben/Grace — forwarding HealthLytics ask. Key asks: 500k token budget, 3-week bake-off, prefer credits vs PO, need logs for evaluation.

Questions for ops/security:
- Can we attach a 30-day credit that maps to a HubSpot deal and has a single audit export?
- Any concerns about sharing anonymized logs for an external competitive evaluation?
- Routing: do we require legal signoff on the attribution clause in our standard credit terms?

I suggested a $25k credit equivalent as a starting point. Ben — any objections to the amount given typical benchmark consumption? Grace — if we approve, would you prefer issuing the grant from the hosted pool or reserved demo bucket (reserved pool helps with SLA assurance)?

On region: they are US-based, low-latency priority.

— Jasmine

> Hi Jasmine,
>
> Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers on sparse-sequence reranking looked promising. ...

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: trial funding and allocation for bake-off vs ZephyrAI

Jasmine — quick read and OK from my side. A few operational notes:

- Amount: $25k seems reasonable for the stated scope. Historically 400–600k token runs at similar settings land in this band.
- Pool: recommend issuing from the hosted eval credit pool (keeps accounting clean) but apply a soft SLA clause in the grant (we can offer a 99.5% availability for the evaluation window). Reserved demo bucket has limited availability this quarter.
- Logs: security can provide an anonymized audit export (no PII). Need security review sign-off; I'll loop them in after we confirm allocation.
- Rate limiting: we should attach a per-second rate cap to prevent noisy-parallel runs from exhausting tokens unintentionally. I suggest 30 rps per model route with burst protection.

Grace — can you confirm the mechanistic steps to create the credit mapped to HubSpot (deal HL-2026-0912) and the timeline to have this live? If we can turn this around within two business days, we should be fine for their kickoff next week.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
